identity.title: Integrated Characterization of AP-2delta Reveals Distinct Regulatory Architecture in Lung Adenocarcinoma and Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

content.abstract: Background/Objectives: AP-2delta, encoded by TFAP2D, is one of the least characterized members of the AP-2 transcription factor family, although available evidence suggests biologically relevant roles in lung cancer that have not yet been thoroughly examined. The aim of the present study was to provide an integrated characterization of AP-2delta/TFAP2D in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC). Methods: LUAD and LUSC data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas. The analysis comprised the expression profiling of AP-2delta target genes, survival-guided TFAP2D stratification, clinical profiling, differential expression and intersection analyses, methylation-derived chromatin compartment profiling, TFAP2D-associated cofactor rewiring, and genome-wide enrichment of AP-2delta targets. In parallel, pocket prioritization was performed using an AlphaFold model of AP-2delta with cross-tool consensus mapping. Results: TFAP2D stratification delineated biologically-distinct states in both histological subtypes (LUAD and LUSC). AP-2delta target genes showed subtype-specific expression patterns and functional organization. The consistent survival association was observed for progression-free interval rather than uniformly across all endpoints. Clinical profiling was more closely associated with molecular subtype composition than broad clinicopathological differences. Differential expression analyses identified both shared and histology-dependent programs associated with TFAP2D. In the chromatin-compartment analysis, LUSC showed a broader and more coherent footprint, whereas LUAD displayed more selective cofactor rewiring. Structure-based analysis prioritized a small set of reproducible candidate pockets concentrated within ordered regions of the TF_AP-2 domain. Conclusions: AP-2delta marks biologically meaningful but histologically non-uniform regulatory states in lung cancer. These findings provide an integrated framework for understanding TFAP2D-dependent regulation in LUAD and LUSC, highlighting AP-2delta as a candidate for future mechanistic and translational investigation.
